why: Count what a fake screenshot never has: 13 sidebar rows, 4 questions that stream word by word through Reading notes, Writing and Answered states, 15 attributed passages and 72 seeded waveform bars; each numbered citation updates the source header, playhead and highlighted transcript row together, and one 'Not in your notes' line per answer states what the data cannot support.

Seven rows per question across six grid columns (rank, tonal square, speaker, note and timestamp, bar, share): hierarchy comes from one inverted selected row and three blue steps that fall to grey at 0%, shares sum to 100 on all four tabs, and passages read but unused stay visible so the table shows what was left out.

Four complete states share one 560px window: 8 transcript lines with a running clock, 12-bar meter and word-by-word typing; a 7-sentence note wired to 7 source passages; 10 tasks across 5 columns with 2 'Needs owner' gaps; and a 7-row plan diff where struck old values, plain new values and dim 'Unchanged' cells show what moved before any row is read.

Nine hairline cells instead of cards: 4 registration crosses mark the inner corners, 8 three-tone glyphs are drawn per feature, each feature ends in a proof row built from six element types (status dot, avatars with '3 of 3 matched', tags, struck corrections, a share key, a 10-bar spark with timecode), the ninth cell is a hatched link out, and hover inverts cell and glyph by swapping CSS variables.

Each of the 3 stats has 5 layers of provenance: named authors, the figure with a blue source mark, one exact sentence on what was measured, a link card to the paper, and a 100-dot thumbnail filled to the same figure (34, 6, 31), so the number is shown twice and can be checked, unlike a bare '10k+ users' tile.
